text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 0.82% today, extending a two-week rally that's added 11.2% to the stock price. The main driver is a sharp reversal in oil market sentiment: crude prices have slid significantly this week after U.S. sanctions relief on Russian energy raised hopes of increased supply hitting the market. Refiners like Marathon benefit when crude input costs fall relative to the value of finished products like gasoline and diesel they produce.

This move caps a volatile stretch that began with geopolitical risk premium baked in—fears of Iran escalating attacks on shipping and potential U.S. strikes pushed crude sharply higher earlier in the week, which initially pressured refiner margins. The sanctions relief news appears to have broken that tension, sending oil back down and improving the outlook for refinery profitability; at the same time, U.S. refineries are running at a healthy 93.5% utilization rate with ample product inventories on hand, supporting steady demand conditions for their output.
